filament.name: Bambu PLA Basic Orange + Bambu PLA Glow

datums.A: Base bottom (primary). Print bed for the stand.

fits_mm.running_rollers: +0.40 diametral PLA-on-PLA for parts printed separately and assembled (rollers on both races). Slicer XY hole compensation stays 0.
fits_mm.pip_cage_pockets: +0.80 diametral (2 nozzles) for same-plate PIP. Assembled running +0.40 is 0.20/side and welds if the roller and cage print in the same layer.
fits_mm.friction_square_drive_and_cage: +0.16 diametral — tap-in locate of the axle on the square post. Not a press. Functional land starts above a 0.80 mm bed lead-in. The rotor cup must NOT friction-fit the rollers.
fits_mm.thrust_land: Axle sits on the base (stator). Rotor plate sits 0.20 above the axle flange (thrust). Rollers sit on the plate top (cup floor). 0.20 axial float at running lands. Retainer is a washer that covers the open cup (OD between cup ID and cup OD).
fits_mm.do_not_nest_cup_pip: Do not print the cup around the PIP rollers on the plate. Race-to-roller at +0.40 is 0.10 mm/side — they fuse. The cup is integral to the rotor; cage+rollers are the PIP cluster dropped in after. Axial capture is the axle flange + retainer, not a top lip (that kills PIP).

lessons.title: Start from a blank document
lessons.teach: cad_new_project first. solid_scene must show 0 bodies before the first extrude. Do not continue a recovered or older Print Kit Tutor (tan nest, red disc, leftover helix planes). Hide construction planes and finished loft sketches before save so File → Open is the five-part kit, not orange datums.

lessons.title: Fits are per role and material
lessons.teach: Fits are per role *and* per whether the parts share a plate. Assembled running (rollers on races printed as other bodies) is +0.40. Same-plate PIP (cage pockets) is +0.80 — two nozzles — or the first layers weld. Slip +0.28. Friction +0.16 on a land *above* a 0.80 mm bed lead-in; a bed-printed friction hole with no relief will not assemble after elephant foot. Model 0.20 axial float at every running land. Cage height matches roller height. Do not nest the cup around the PIP rollers on the plate.

lessons.title: Snug is not a press
lessons.teach: FDM press fits fail from elephant foot. Friction locate is still a modeled gap, and the functional land starts above a 2-nozzle lead-in on every bed-printed bore (plate bore, axle square, retainer square). Retain with a flange, land, or retainer — not interference. No metal 608s. No inward top lip over PIP rollers.

lessons.title: Individual parts, then an assembly
lessons.teach: Each body that moves is its own component with exactly one occurrence. assembly_create_component already inserts the root instance — do not create a second copy. Link the stator with rigid joints (axle sits on the base; retainer sits on the post). Revolute the rotor cup and cage on the axle axis, and each roller in its pocket — never a blade-spar face. The rotor cup is the outer race (rotor_spin). There is no separate bushing. Blades stay one printed body with the plate.

lessons.title: Print a roller pack that takes tip moment
lessons.teach: A tall skinny sleeve cannot hold aero loads at the blade tips. A pile of unmatched-height races with no housing cannot either. Matching 8 mm flats is still a pancake stack. Use a large-PCD printed roller cartridge (PIP rollers in a cage, +0.80 pockets) inside a rotor **drum** whose height matches the rollers (≥28 mm at exam scale, 70 mm at scale 1.0) on a ≥5 mm plate. Thrust floor + outer race + blade plate are one frame. Do not PIP the rollers inside the cup at running clearance. The cage is a spacer; axial capture is the flange + retainer. Size rollers for FDM (min Ø8 / h28).

lessons.title: Keep the machine even
lessons.teach: Three helical blades at 120°. Root azimuth 30° so a 60° helix stays balanced. The square post is the stator — the rotor cup freewheels on the roller pack. An odd one-sided vane is not a turbine.

lessons.title: Blades and hub are one part
lessons.teach: The rotor is a single printed body: a ≥5 mm root plate (print sit + thrust), an integral open-top drum (outer race), and a moment web per blade that climbs that drum wall out to the airfoil. The plate is not the load path — a can on a cracker still dumps the overhung moment into a 5 mm disk. First loft station is the plate (flat sit-plane cut). Do not hang blades off skinny arms. Do not ship an 8 mm washer as a cup. Print standing on the plate. Drop the rotor on the axle, then drop the cartridge into the cup.

lessons.title: The section is a 2026-appropriate airfoil
lessons.teach: Directionless VAWTs see reversing α. Build a thick symmetric airfoil (t/c 21–24%, blunt TE ≥ 2 nozzles). Cite NACA 0021. Draft the chord (root > tip) so the standing print needs little support.

lessons.title: Scale is a parameter; 1.0 fills an X2D
lessons.teach: Linear dimensions are the X2D-max design (256×256×260, 8 mm margin). spec.scale shrinks the source (exam default 0.4). Feature sizes that would go below printable (roller Ø8 / h28, TE 0.8, 4-nozzle walls, plate 5 mm) are clamped. noBS-CAD has no document-level scale feature yet — the spec parameter is the source of truth.

lessons.title: Print rotational parts lying down
lessons.teach: Never design a tall skinny shaft that needs a tower of support. The axle is a flanged square puck, printed on the flange. Base, cage, and retainer print flat, each with a 2-nozzle bed lead-in on functional holes. The rotor stands on its root plate so each blade ends on that flat horizontal. Cage+rollers are the PIP cluster; drop the rotor on the axle first, then drop the cartridge into the open-top cup. The cup is not nested around the rollers on the plate.

lessons.title: Helical blades, not a straight fence
lessons.teach: A prismatic extrusion is idle for most of the rev. Loft a closed NACA at ≥2 stations with ≥45° helix. Mid-chord stays on R. Chord stays tangent. Open tips — no end cap.

lessons.title: Ship an assembly drawing
lessons.teach: Create a drawing sheet, auto-layout standard views, and annotate fits, scale, print orientation, and the BOM. A kit without a drawing is not a product.

lessons.title: Publish the design report
lessons.teach: Write the iteration log, airfoil/Re, role-based fits, roller pack, scale vs X2D, finish, BOM, and plastic cost. READY TO PRINT without a costed report is a fail.

lessons.title: Export one laid-out plate
lessons.teach: Wipe Print-Kit-Tutor/ first so leftover five-plate and shaft/hub/wings names are gone. Save the assembled .nbcad, then solid_move_copy parts onto the bed (rotor standing on the deck, others flat) and solid_export_3mf once as 01-kit. Two materials only: PLA Orange and PLA Glow (rotor / cup). Do not export the assembled nest as the print job.
